summary.name: JET Pilot
summary.one_liner: JET Pilot is a free, open-source, native desktop client for managing Kubernetes clusters from kubeconfig files and connected cloud accounts.
use_cases: Switching between many Kubernetes clusters and contexts
Checking GitOps Flux or Argo CD delivery status
Reviewing who can do what with RBAC
Viewing CPU and memory usage history for workloads
Browsing Helm releases and installing charts
Following logs from all pods of a workload at once
summary.what_it_does: JET Pilot lists every cluster from your kubeconfig files and connected cloud accounts (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, DigitalOcean, Akamai, Civo, Scaleway, Vultr, Exoscale) in one hub. It can show tables merged across several contexts and namespaces, with live updates streamed from the API server rather than polling. It includes GitOps views for Flux and Argo CD, CPU and memory history, an RBAC access-review tool, YAML editing with diff and server-side dry run, and Helm release browsing. Credentials are stored in the system keychain, and it has no account or telemetry.
notable: Connects nine cloud providers and finds their clusters automatically
Live table updates streamed from the Kubernetes API server
Built on Rust and Tauri 2 with Vue 3 frontend; MIT licensed
Stores tokens and keys in the system keychain; no account or telemetry
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so macOS may require removing the quarantine flag on first launch (Homebrew install avoids this)
Windows installers are not code-signed, so SmartScreen may warn
Linux ARM64 builds arrive only with a future release; glibc 2.35+ required for the Linux build
